name: Epidermolysis Bullosa Simplex with Anodontia/Hypodontia
aliases: Epidermolysis Bullosa Simplex with Dental Anomalies

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Genetic Diagnostic Criteria for Epidermolysis Bullosa Simplex with Anodontia/Hypodontia

criteria.description: Recurrent skin blistering and erosions primarily on hands and feet triggered by minor trauma
Congenital absence of some or all teeth (anodontia or hypodontia)
Identification of pathogenic mutations in KRT5 or KRT14 genes
Skin biopsy showing intraepidermal cleavage within basal keratinocytes
Positive family history consistent with autosomal dominant inheritance

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of recurrent skin blistering and dental anomalies with identification of pathogenic keratin gene mutation
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing is essential to confirm diagnosis and differentiate from other EB subtypes.

pathognomonic.notes: Blisters typically localized to acral sites
searchTerms: skin blisters inside epidermis caused by trauma

pathognomonic.notes: Partial or complete absence of teeth
searchTerms: missing or fewer teeth from birth

pathognomonic.notes: Skin erosions and crusting following blister rupture
searchTerms: skin tears easily with little injury

common.notes: Thickened skin on palms and soles
Blistering and erosions in oral cavity
Teeth erupt later than normal developmental milestones

occasional.notes: Localized hair loss due to repeated blistering

searchTerms: mild blisters on palms and soles without scars

rare.notes: Resulting from repeated mucosal blistering and scarring

rare.symptomName: Anemia secondary to chronic mucosal involvement
rare.notes: Due to chronic blood loss or inflammation
searchTerms: low blood count due to mucosal problems

laboratory: Normal routine blood tests unless secondary complications
imaging: Dental radiographs showing hypodontia or anodontia
genetic: Pathogenic variants in KRT5 or KRT14 genes
other: Skin biopsy immunofluorescence mapping confirming intraepidermal blistering

distinguishingFeatures: Blistering occurs at the level of lamina lucida

redFlags: Extensive mucosal involvement causing feeding difficulties
Signs of secondary infection or sepsis
Severe dental agenesis impacting nutrition and development
references: Fine JD, et al. Inherited epidermolysis bullosa: updated recommendations on diagnosis and classification. J Am Acad Dermatol. 2014.
Orphanet Report Series: Epidermolysis Bullosa Simplex with Anodontia/Hypodontia. Orphanet. 2020.
